ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $2.74 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexempted detour distance on the 09:47–09:53 off-route segment, per NS-7; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI service: the fare record builds the $29.11 charge from base $3.90 + $18.50 distance over 13.12 km + $5.24 time over 20.2 min + $1.47 platform, waiting $0.00, no surge [F6][F5], so RD-2 puts the remedy in metered distance only, not in the fixed-fare/added-fee branch of FARE-1 [RD-2].

The GPS record identifies exactly one off-route segment, 09:47–09:53, running 3.83 km where the optimal route covers 1.89 km, adding 1.94 km and straying up to 777 m from the optimal route [F3], against a whole-trip actual of 13.1 km versus 10.7 km optimal [F1]. That segment is an unexempted deviation under RD-1, which sets no percentage or kilometre threshold [RD-1].

No exemption applies. The chat record is complete and contains a single message, the rider's 09:35 kerbside message naming the pick-up point (Mandarin Gallery kerb, red jacket) and saying nothing about the route [F7][F8]; it therefore consists of no rider agreement at all before the 09:47–09:53 segment, and my reading of that message is a pick-up arrangement, not a route instruction [RD-5]. The driver's explanation, made after the trip and outside the chat — "I followed my GPS; it rerouted me" — is not a rider message and cannot be consent [F9][RD-5]. RD-3(a) does not assist either: the only place ever named by the rider is the pick-up kerb, and, per the trace, no stop was measured in this segment, so the driver's own choice of path produced the off-route kilometres [F7][F3][RD-3].

RD-4 gives no cover: there were no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window [F12], and the only speed-band records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Ayer Rajah Expressway and Kent Ridge Road [F10][F11], which are neither band 1 nor band 2 and in any case are only corroborative and never a standalone exemption; the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain [F13][RD-4].

Amount: the fare record fixes this trip's per-kilometre rate as distance fare ÷ distance km, $18.50 ÷ 13.12 km = $1.4101/km [F4][F6]. The unexempted segment's extra distance is 1.94 km [F3], so 1.94 km × $1.4101/km = $2.7356, rounded to $2.74 [RD-2]. The fare record's own excess-distance line of $3.44 (2.44 km) [F4] is not awarded: RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segments' extra km, and the 0.50 km gap between 2.44 km and 1.94 km is unassigned corridor mileage that is expressly not refundable [F4][F3][RD-2]. Waiting time is $0.00 and is not in issue [F6].

No account flag: the route-branch count is zero and the single prior upheld dispute is not route-related [F15], so RD-6's "repeated" condition for a route-deviation flag is not met, and profile facts could not decide the route finding in any event [RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the rider's 09:35 message, the only chat message [F7][F8], the driver's post-trip statement [F9] and the complaint, and found no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the chat record is complete with every message timestamped [F8], the segment is measured by GPS [F3], and the fare arithmetic rests on the fare record [F4][F6].

segment_findings.reason: The complete chat holds one message only, the rider's 09:35 kerbside message naming the pick-up point and no road [F7][F8], so no rider message precedes the 09:47–09:53 segment; the driver's post-trip statement that his GPS rerouted him is not rider consent [F9]. Ground stipulated by both advocates: consent_after_or_none → counts [RD-5][RD-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's arithmetic that the ride is '1.56 km shorter than the distance billed on top of the estimate' is not supported: the record bills 13.12 km of metered distance against a 13.1 km actual track [F1][F6], and the fare record's excess-distance line is 2.44 km [F4]. RD-2 refunds measured unexempted segment extra km only [RD-2].

The claim's own figure is accepted ($2.74) but only as computed here from the fare record's rate $18.50 ÷ 13.12 = $1.4101/km applied to the segment's 1.94 km [F4][F6][F3]; the record's labelled excess of $3.44 (2.44 km) [F4] is not refundable corridor mileage under RD-2 [RD-2].
No account flag is available on this record: the flag requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days [F15], and RD-6 also bars profile facts from deciding the route finding [RD-6].

The driver's no-flag conclusion is accepted, but not for the reason that his 2 disputes with 1 upheld across 90 days are harmless in principle; the operative fact is route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F15], so RD-6's repeated-breach condition fails [RD-6].

The rider's profile (1 dispute, 0 upheld, 0 route) [F14] is irrelevant to this ruling; profile facts may not decide the route finding, which rests on the GPS segment [F3][F1] and the fare record [F4][F6] [RD-6][RD-2].

Accepted as far as it goes, but the rider's recalled '11 km' figure plays no part in the award; the record figure is 10.7 km optimal versus 13.1 km actual [F1][F3], and the refund is computed from the measured segment alone [RD-2].
